architecture_decision.reason: The existing fsqlite package is the preferred non-duplicative placement, but comparative package evidence, the complete graph matrix, accepted owner contract, native/io-uring feature split, and toolchain disposition are unresolved. DEP-ADR-010 therefore keeps asupersync[sqlite] and rusqlite as the supported path.

preferred_candidate.selection_rationale: A precursor integration seam already exists under this package and namespace, so it is the lowest-duplication provisional starting point. Whether the official adapter belongs here or in a second fsqlite-asupersync package remains deferred until graph, release-owner, and discoverability comparison.
preferred_candidate.required_native_feature_contract: Before async-api may forward native, fsqlite-vfs/native must stop forwarding linux-asupersync-uring and the Linux io-uring dependency must become optional under that explicit platform feature. Otherwise the production adapter must declare and obtain owner acceptance for the io-uring edge.
preferred_candidate.current_linux_native_observation: fsqlite/native forwards fsqlite-vfs/native; fsqlite-vfs/native forwards linux-asupersync-uring; and io-uring is an unconditional Linux target dependency at the observed revision.
preferred_candidate.public_context_requirement: Every official async operation must take &asupersync::Cx as its first non-receiver argument. The current fsqlite_types::cx::Cx plus ambient NativeCx::current or Runtime::current_handle lookup is not the accepted end state.
preferred_candidate.worker_requirement: Any dedicated worker thread, stack allocation, command admission, abandonment, interrupt, drain, and shutdown behavior must be declared and proved by the I2 lifecycle beads before implementation is accepted.

support_lifecycle.required_policy: Each fsqlite release must publish its supported Asupersync interval, minimum Rust version, target set, deprecation window, and rollback version. At least the current and immediately previous compatible pair remain in CI for one fsqlite minor-release interval.
support_lifecycle.incumbent_policy: asupersync[sqlite] remains supported and is not deprecated while the adapter policy or evidence is incomplete.

version_and_toolchain_contract.candidate_nightly_requirement: The observed x86_64 graph unconditionally reaches fsqlite-btree and fsqlite-pager core_intrinsics feature gates; Windows also reaches windows_by_handle. Current FrankenSQLite documentation requires nightly.
version_and_toolchain_contract.nightly_policy: The adapter must not enable Asupersync's default nightly-outcome-try feature. Before I1 closes, owners must either accept and date-pin a shared nightly because FrankenSQLite source requires it, or require a stable-source refactor. A floating nightly and the bare Rust 1.85 declaration are not an accepted support contract.
compatibility_rules: a supported consumer resolves one asupersync package ID from one source
the lowest and highest declared compatible Asupersync versions both compile in neutral-consumer CI
a breaking Cx or cancellation-contract change requires a coordinated compatibility update before either release is advertised
an unpublished path, git patch, or dirty checkout is evidence-only and cannot define a supported version interval

graph_evidence_contract.proc_macro_method: Derive proc-macro packages from cargo metadata target.kind; cargo tree has no proc-macro edge selector.
graph_evidence_contract.receipt_rule: Every supported row needs immutable revisions, manifest and lockfile SHA-256 digests, exact command, host and target triples, toolchain, feature set, package IDs by dependency kind, build-script and proc-macro package sets derived from metadata, Tokio/native classifications, exit code, and terminal timestamp.

prerequisite_evidence.conclusion: DEP-ADR-010 keeps the incumbent and forbids a reverse edge.
The historical proposal added 33 unique crates; a naive combined consumer duplicated Asupersync; a patch unified it.
A standalone evidence-only consumer can resolve one Asupersync package and execute one retained parity vector.

blocking_gaps.detail: No current immutable normal/dev/build receipts or metadata-derived proc-macro classifications exist for the minimum profile matrix, and the owner target/version allowsets are not accepted.
blocking_gaps.unblock: Generate every required coordinate from clean immutable revisions and attach manifest, lockfile, metadata, tree, classification, and terminal command receipts.

blocking_gaps.detail: Repository-level responsibilities are proposed, but no named owner has accepted release and support responsibility.
blocking_gaps.unblock: Record named owner approval and the support lifecycle in the I1 bead thread.

blocking_gaps.detail: The desired async-api to native forwarding currently implies linux-asupersync-uring, and io-uring is an unconditional Linux target dependency.
blocking_gaps.unblock: Accept the Linux io-uring edge explicitly or approve a downstream feature split that makes the dependency optional and keeps the base native adapter distinct.

blocking_gaps.detail: Current x86_64 and Windows source requires nightly despite the bare Rust 1.85 declaration, and the repository toolchain floats.
blocking_gaps.unblock: Approve a date-pinned shared nightly requirement or require a stable-source refactor; record the decision without enabling nightly-outcome-try on the Asupersync dependency.

downstream_implementation_gates.requirement: Replace the current fsqlite_types::cx::Cx plus ambient native-runtime lookup with one official &asupersync::Cx boundary.
Prove interrupt, drain, response abandonment, worker join, and bounded shutdown before the adapter is supported.
Exercise the release order and publish the version/support contract after I1 selects the architecture.

It does not prove any current FrankenSQLite graph, compile, runtime, cancellation, portability, parity, performance, publication, owner acceptance, support interval, or release readiness. It authorizes no source implementation, dependency change, feature deprecation, cutover, or bead closure.
